sections.title: Form and habitat
sections.text: A solitary cactus from the central Mexican plateau, with a globose stem that becomes columnar, marked by ribs and white flecks. Large plants may reach about 160 cm tall and 30 cm across. Its yellow flowers are about 5–7 cm wide; it grows on rocky, dry slopes.

sections.title: Food and image
sections.text: No edible use was established in the sources consulted. The plate shows the ribbed, flecked body, spines and yellow flower and is consistent with this species.

sections.title: Related cactus
sections.text: Astrophytum caput-medusae is another Mexican congener, but its buried base and long narrow tubercles create a very different silhouette.
